title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East on 1968-06-14
lineage: AUD > MC > R > R > PCM > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Lo‑fi audience tape that captures a ferocious Fillmore East debut – blistering 24‑minute “Caution”, feedback sandwich opener/closer and wild transitions make the performance legendary despite muddy sound.
ai_review.review: The June 1968 Fillmore East show is hailed as one of the most intense early Dead concerts, highlighted by an epic 24‑minute “Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks)”, relentless feedback openings, and rare Space > The Eleven > St. Stephen transitions.  The audience recording is decidedly lo‑fi – drums and Phil’s bass are often buried, vocals clip, and the mix is oversaturated – but Jerry’s guitar cuts through and the raw energy shines through for fans who prize performance over fidelity.

ai_rating.rationale: Average star rating from reviewers is ~4.7, with most praising the show’s historic intensity and unique setlist while consistently noting poor audio quality; weighting performance (70%) over recording (30%) yields a strong overall score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Oversaturated tape with muddy drums, clipped vocals and limited bass presence; Jerry’s guitar remains clear.  Typical 1968 AUD limitations but surprisingly listenable after acclimation.

standout_songs: Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks) – ~24 min
show_quality.setlist_flow: A feedback‑sandwich framing the set, with daring transitions (Space→Eleven→St Stephen) and a coherent yet wild progression that captures the band’s primal 1968 energy.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Dominant throughout; his guitar is loud, often the only clearly audible instrument, described as ‘on another plane.’
band_member_comments.Phil: Barely audible on this tape; reviewers note his bass is lost in the mix.
band_member_comments.Bob: Vocals and harp are largely buried; occasional mention of his presence during Caution.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drums are muffled or inaudible for much of the show, making rhythm hard to discern.
